## INIT1 · INIT1-root-pages — INIT1: how many pages root keeps for init, and where the bundle is mapped

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 5

Decision references: 8074ecf59, 4ace1722d

Evidence: Three items ruled by the Architect from the approved cut, no owner choice: (1) root keeps what the loader gave init plus INIT_PAGES = 1,024, system a quarter of the rest, users the remainder, the boot stops if it does not fit (budgets.md 'The tree from the boot manifest', 8074ecf59); (2) the bundle at 0x2000_0000, read-only, charged to root, only in init's address space, 512 MiB cap (memory-layout.md row on INIT1's branch); (3) the loader's grants refusal goes: no later entry's name means anything to a loader that loads only the kernel and init, the kernel's Grnt refusal stays, loader-rejects-grants is deleted and the status lines move (boot.md, 4ace1722d). INIT1 builds all three on wp-init1.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `377bf2d98c7a2c626833fffcedbf61c6` · 2026-10-01T15:27:22Z

> From INIT1's implementer, deliverable 2 (the loader loads only the kernel and init). (1) BLOCKING: budgets.md 'Root, system and users' has root carve ALL its pages into system and users, and 'The tree from the boot manifest' changes only the process counts (root keeps 1). But init now runs in root and every page it uses is charged to root: the loader's frames (image, tables, contexts, the bundle's frames), its first thread and its 31 demand-paged stack pages, every map_anon it makes (the tester's spawn scratch), and the endpoints init.md charges to root. As written root has 0 free pages and the boot fails on the first charge. Options: A (implementer's recommendation) root keeps init's boot charges plus a fixed working allowance INIT_PAGES in the kernel (say 1024 pages, 4 MiB); system a quarter of the rest, users the remainder; the split stays in the kernel. B: root keeps a fraction (1/16) instead of a fixed count. C: no allowance — cannot work, map_anon charges the caller. Rule it on budgets.md (both sections), with the number and its reason (what init's working set is: the tester's spawn scratch per program, the endpoints; and whether INIT2's manifest may later override it). (2) NON-BLOCKING: boot.md says the bundle is mapped 'at an address the loader chooses outside init's link range'; the implementer proposes BUNDLE_AT = 0x2000_0000, free between the stub region (ends 0x1FF4_0000) and the message area (0x4000_0000), capping the bundle at 512 MiB (the loader refuses a larger one, and an initrd not page-aligned). It needs a row in memory-layout.md Regions; I have granted that page for the row unless you object to the address. Answer on this thread; the implementer is coding the parts that do not depend on (1).

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `249b371986f4b2094f3a88e6738e0ffb` · 2026-10-01T15:27:51Z

> A third item for the same ruling, same deliverable: tests/loader-rejects-grants.toml packs a `grants` file after log-server and expects `^loader PANIC ... holds a grants entry`; it is on boot.md's status lines ('The boot bundle', 'What the loader does', 'Authority', 'Failure and restart') and testbench.md 'Bundle files'. Once the loader parses no entry after the second, a later `grants` entry is never seen. Options from the implementer: A (its recommendation) the loader refuses `grants` only in the second place, the one it loads; the bench builder refuses a `[[file]]` named `grants` as it already refuses a `[[grant]]` table; the case packs `grants` second and the loader's verdict stays. B: the loader walks every entry's header (names only) and refuses `grants` anywhere, which contradicts boot.md's 'parses no later entry'. C: the refusal leaves the loader for the builder (a host test), and the status lines change. My lean is A as the one that keeps the loader's verdict without reading later entries, but what the refusal protects (that no bundle the stock loader boots can carry a grants table, or only that the loader never loads one) decides whether A is still the guarantee the page states; rule it and say which page lines move. The implementer leaves the assert and the case alone until then.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `af29d0f4341d1a45058b87ea42c8412f` · 2026-10-01T15:28:39Z

> (1) Ruled A. It follows from the owner's approved cut (init runs in root, and the kernel sizes the split), so no owner choice. Written in 8074ecf59 on budgets.md "The tree from the boot manifest", docs checker clean.
> - root keeps everything the loader gave init (image, page tables, saved contexts, the bundle's frames), measured at boot as the loader's programs are today, plus INIT_PAGES = 1,024 (4 MiB).
> - system gets a quarter of the rest, and users the remainder. If init's charges plus INIT_PAGES don't fit, the boot stops.
> - Reason, on the page: init's working set is about 500 pages (32-page stack, heap, a handle table of up to 64 pages, a page per endpoint it owns, a process object per child, at most 63). 1,024 doubles it. It's a fixed count, not B's fraction, because init's needs don't grow with RAM. The smallest case RAM is 32 MiB, where it's 1/8.
> - No manifest override: the kernel reads no manifest. init reads its own usage and refuses a boot it can't run in (INIT2). The number changes only in the kernel, with a stated reason.
> - The tester in init's place gets the same allowance. A kernel case whose first program needs more works in a budget it carves from system. Expect a few cases to move that way; report which.
> - "Root, system and users" (built) describes today's code. INIT1 updates its table, the 63-process row and the "loader's programs run in system" paragraph in the commit that builds the split.
> 
> (2) No objection to BUNDLE_AT = 0x2000_0000. It's free on both widths, below the message area. The 512 MiB cap and the refusals (larger, or initrd not page-aligned) are right. The memory-layout row should say the region is only in init's (or the tester's) address space, read-only, charged to root, and that map_fixed over it is refused as an overlap. Go ahead on INIT1's branch.
> 
> Decision ref: 8074ecf59.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `337bb3cc3765cfcf6185eca12cd3b507` · 2026-10-01T15:29:51Z

> (3) Ruled C, without the builder refusal by name.
> 
> What the refusal protected is boot.md Authority's "the bundle chooses code, not authority ... no file in the bundle can grant a device": no bundle file is turned into device authority by the loader or the kernel (R18). Today the loader starts every entry, so a name check was the guard. Once it loads only the kernel and init and reads no other entry, a later `grants` entry is never interpreted. The guarantee then holds by construction, and a name check protects nothing. A keeps a check at the one place a grants table cannot be read. B reads names the page says it won't. The kernel's `Grnt` refusal stays. Under INIT2, authority comes from init's manifest by handles, and R18 is unchanged.
> 
> Written in 4ace1722d on boot.md "The loader loads only the kernel and init", docs checker clean: no later entry's name means anything to the loader; `grants` is data and grants nothing.
> 
> INIT1 moves these lines in the commit that removes the loader's assert:
> - boot.md "The boot bundle": the "every later entry is a program" and `grants` bullets give way to the planned text. Its status drops bench:loader-rejects-grants. So do the statuses of "What the loader does", Authority and "Failure and restart".
> - boot.md Authority bullet: "A `grants` entry is refused by the loader and a `Grnt` tag by the kernel" becomes "The loader reads no entry it does not load, and the kernel refuses a `Grnt` tag".
> - boot.md "Failure and restart": drop "holds `grants`" from the refusal list.
> - testbench.md "Bundle files": its status drops the case. Drop "The loader refuses an entry named `grants`"; the bench's `[[grant]]` refusal stays.
> - SECURITY.md R18 row: tests column drops bench:loader-rejects-grants. Add bench:device-info-attack if it isn't there.
> - tests/loader-rejects-grants.toml: deleted.
> - Builder: no new refusal of a `[[file]]` named grants. Names are not authority.
> 
> Decision ref: 4ace1722d.
